rounds.text: The intrinsic value derived from a discounted cash flow model stands at ₹828 per share, establishing a substantial margin of safety of 30.0% relative to the current market price of ₹580 [E45, E46]. Furthermore, fundamental momentum is exceptionally strong, backed by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 23% [E17], a compounded profit growth of 38% [E21], and robust cash conversion where operating cash flow reached ₹214 Cr, fully backing reported profits at 1.83x [E34, E35]. Institutional support is expanding concurrently, evidenced by positive money flow and increased holdings from both foreign and domestic institutions [E42, E43, E44], alongside a strong technical posture with a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51]. Conceded: promoter holding has decreased over recent quarters [E41, E61] and compounded sales and profit growth over a three-year window experienced minor contractions [E16, E20].

The bear case highlights that underlying long-term growth has stagnated, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of -2% [E16] and compounded profit growth of -4% [E20], alongside a poor 5-year sales growth rate of 10.7% [E62]. Short-term margin pressure is evident as quarterly operating margin declined to 16% in September 2026 from 18% in the year-ago quarter [-2 pp] [E31], with rule-based screening explicitly flagging decelerating earnings growth [E71]. Insiders are de-risking heavily, demonstrated by promoter holding dropping from 68.15% in December 2023 to 58.47% in September 2026 (-9.68 percentage points) [E41], accompanied by a further single-quarter reduction flag of -7.31% [E61]. Working capital inefficiency remains a structural drag with high debtors of 151 days [E65], while historical volatility is severe, carrying a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -75.6% [E53]. Furthermore, price performance has significantly detached from delivery, with recent price growth exceeding profit growth by 47% [E57]. Conceded: the company maintains a solid balance sheet with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.19x [E37], strong TTM cash conversion of 1.83x [E34], and positive institutional buying momentum [+2.75 percentage points] [E44].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth is negative at -2% [E16], 3-year profit growth is -4% [E20], and 5-year sales growth is 10.7% [E62]. However, focusing purely on those historical troughs ignores a massive acceleration in the trailing twelve months, where sales grew by 23% [E17] and profits surged by 38% [E21]. While quarterly operating margin dipped by 2 percentage points year-over-year in September 2026 [E31], the longer-term operating margin has actually expanded by 3 percentage points compared to three years earlier [E30]. Conceded: promoters reduced holdings to 58.47% [E41], [E61], but institutional investors have aggressively stepped in with positive money flow of +2.75 percentage points [E44], led by foreign institutions increasing stakes to 3.37% [E42] and domestic institutions rising to 12.67% [E43]. Furthermore, the bear's concern over historical drawdown [-75.6%] [E53] is countered by robust operational fundamentals, including a high TTM cash conversion of 1.83x [E34] producing Rs 214 Cr in operating cash flow [E35], paired with a conservatively managed balance sheet where borrowings decreased to Rs 203 Cr [E39].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales grew by 23% [E17] and profits surged by 38% [E21]. However, relying on this recent acceleration ignores the structural reality of poor multi-year performance, including a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -2% [E16], a 3-year profit decline of -4% [E20], and a weak 5-year sales growth rate of 10.7% [E62]. Conceded: institutional money flow shows an increase [E44], but this comes alongside a severe and ongoing dilution of promoter commitment, with holdings dropping precipitously by 9.68 percentage points down to 58.47% [E41], including a further 7.31% drop noted last quarter [E61]. Furthermore, pointing to operating margin expansion over a three-year span [E30] glosses over recent deteriorating trends, specifically an inconsistent yearly profile [E32], an inconsistent quarterly trend [E33], and a margin contraction of 2 percentage points in September 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E31]. Finally, strong operating cash flow [E35] does not erase the systemic risk of high debtors stretching to 151 days [E65], nor does it protect investors from historical volatility that has triggered a catastrophic peak-to-trough drawdown of -75.6% [E53].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales contraction of -2% [E16] and profit decline of -4% [E20], alongside an inconsistent quarterly margin trend [E33]. However, this multi-year view ignores the powerful cyclical inflection underway, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth accelerating to 23% [E17] and profit growth surging to 38% [E21], with rules-based screen scoring 88/100 as a buy [E66]. Conceded: promoter holding dropped by 9.68 percentage points to 58.47% [E41], but this insider adjustment has been aggressively absorbed by institutional accumulation, with foreign and domestic institutions increasing their stakes and driving positive institutional money flow [E42, E43, E44]. Conceded: operating margins contracted by 2 percentage points in September 2026 [E31] and debtors stand at 151 days [E65], but these friction points are dwarfed by robust operational cash generation of ₹ 214 Cr and exceptional cash conversion of 1.83x ensuring profits are fully backed by cash [E34, E35]. Finally, citing a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -75.6% [E53] ignores the present technical and fundamental reality: the stock trades above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50], is supported by a sector tailwind score of +0.60 [E74], and benefits from proactive capital investments such as expanding rooftop solar capacity to 6 MW to optimize cost control and structural efficiency [E81, E83].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 23% [E17] and profit growth hit 38% [E21], but these short-term figures are completely offset by the multi-year reality of a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -2% [E16], a profit decline of -4% [E20], and a poor 5-year sales growth rate of 10.7% [E62]. Conceded: institutional holdings increased [E42, E43, E44], but this cannot obscure the significant structural insider exodus wherein promoter holding has plummeted by 9.68 percentage points down to 58.47% [E41], compounded by a sharp sequential drop last quarter alone [E61]. Conceded: cash generation reached Rs 214 Cr with 1.83x conversion [E34, E35], yet operational efficiency remains structurally constrained by severely high debtors stretching to 151 days [E65] and an inconsistent yearly and quarterly margin trend [E32, E33]. Finally, while the bull dismisses the historical -75.6% drawdown [E53], the present fundamental profile is weighed down by a low return on equity of 12.6% over the last 3 years [E63] and a meager dividend payout of just 10.5% of profits [E64].
